title: Low Tide: Wrack Line
statement: The tide leaves its signature where it stopped: a line of weed, drawn in one long uneven stroke across the sand, highest where the water reached furthest. This is that line, seen from above, with the wet below it and the dry above. The weed is kelp, torn from a holdfast somewhere out past the picture, and I have drawn it the way I draw everything, as a thing that grew from one point and branched: the frond on the left is still attached to its holdfast, a knot of root-like fingers, and from there the line runs rightward, thinning, until it is only a scatter of small shells and a last strand. The sea writes this line twice a day and never the same way. Whoever comes next can bring the water back over it, or let it dry and curl.
process: I laid down a dry sand field above and a darker wet field below, separated by a slow uneven curve, and drew the wrack along that curve as hand-drawn fronds branching from a single holdfast at the left, each frond a tapering path with small bladders, with the forms thinning to shells and fragments toward the right. The line is the only structure in the picture.
